solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Forfeited allotment, perhaps, having failed to keep up

definitions.meaning: literally, having lost one's patch of rented garden ground, an allotment being a small plot
idiomatically, having become confused and lost track of what is going on

explanation.surface: A gardener loses their allotment for not keeping up with the weeding or the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small plot of council land rented for growing vegetables, common in Britain; the idiom means to lose one's grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the idiom: a literal loss of a garden patch, and the figurative sense of losing one's grasp on events.

clue.text: Escape difficult situation — it can relieve gloom

parts.note: on the lam means on the run, so lam is escape
a plight is a predicament

explanation.surface: Getting out of a tight spot can lift one's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gloom' reads as low mood, but it is darkness lifted by a street lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from lamps literally lifts darkness, the physical sense of gloom.

clue.text: Astaire regularly appearing to eat fish

indicators.note: every second letter of the dancer's name is taken at regular intervals

parts.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Fred Astaire turns up regularly for a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of ASTAIRE give SAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish of the herring family, often tinned, is one kind of fish.

clue.text: Disorganised tours on Med, say — United having pre-match collection

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged letters sit on top of the sea
the letters of the word tours are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the Mediterranean is an example of a sea
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A shambolic Mediterranean tour by Manchester United before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pre-match' sounds like football but means before a wedding; the anagram gives TROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's set of clothes and linen gathered before her marriage, a match being a wedding.

clue.text: Old and new technology's outlets

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former or old
IT, information technology, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: Electrical sockets for both outdated and modern devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Ways out of a place are its outlets, in the sense of openings for leaving.

clue.text: Medicine for the ear brought you and me together

indicators.note: the phrase is meant to be heard, so a word that sounds like it is wanted

parts.note: linked us means joined the two of us

explanation.surface: A cure for earache made the two of us friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the ear' looks like ear drops but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing syrupy cough mixture is a liquid medicine.

clue.text: One in receiving line thanks king and queen

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A guest in a royal receiving line thanks the monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: A receiving line usually greets guests; here it is the line of work of those who take.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts or takes something is in the business of receiving.

clue.text: Bone from big bird found in middle of seafront

indicators.note: the bird is located within the central letters, so one piece sits inside the other
the central pair of letters of the eight-letter word seafront is taken

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A bird's bone is discovered halfway along the promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: With an even-length word, 'middle of' takes the central pair of letters (FR); 'found in' then signals the bird sitting between them. 'big' is just there to point at a large bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone of the leg is a specific example of a bone, the longest in the human body.

clue.text: Release activist, one with potential to destabilise cell?

definitions.text: one with potential to destabilise cell?

parts.note: to free is to release
a radical is a political activist

explanation.surface: Freeing a political prisoner who might stir up trouble in a terrorist cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' suggests a prison or terrorist cell; it is a biological cell.
explanation.definitionFit: An unstable atom or molecule with an unpaired electron that can damage living tissue, a chemistry term.

clue.text: Lily perhaps producing thin paper

definitions.meaning: read as a possessive phrase, a lily is a relative of a common bulb vegetable, both in the lily family
a translucent, very light writing paper

explanation.surface: A lily somehow yields delicate paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer (5'1,3) to read ONION'S KIN: the lily is a botanical relative of the onion. 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is the name for a thin, glossy, translucent paper once used for carbon copies and airmail letters.

clue.text: Luxury Caribbean island boss offering protection for head's supporter

parts.note: Necker Island is Richard Branson's private luxury island in the British Virgin Islands
a chief is a boss

explanation.surface: A tycoon's island boss provides protection for a headteacher's backer.
explanation.walkthrough: The head's supporter is the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth tied around the throat protects the part of the body that holds up the head.

clue.text: Caught in ecstasy, hides cream cakes

indicators.note: the cricket letter for caught goes inside the combined other pieces

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
hides are dens or lairs where animals or hunters conceal themselves
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone high on ecstasy is caught concealing pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' looks like a verb but is a plural noun, LAIRS; C goes between E and LAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Choux pastry fingers filled with cream and topped with chocolate are a classic kind of cream cake.

clue.text: Lecherous comic, one going for unknown

indicators.note: the letter for one departs and an algebraic unknown takes its place

parts.note: satiric means mocking or comic in a biting way
I is the Roman numeral one
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A comedian with a lewd act is replaced by someone nobody has heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the I of SATIRIC for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs were lustful woodland creatures of Greek myth, so behaviour like theirs is lustful and lewd.

clue.text: Naughty, debauched man pinching underwear with no strings attached

indicators.note: the debauched man grabs and holds the underwear letter within himself

parts.note: a roué is a dissolute, debauched man
a G-string is skimpy underwear; remove the strings and only the G remains

explanation.surface: A lecher steals knickers, keeping things casual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no strings attached' looks like the definition (free, unattached) but trims G-STRING to G, which goes inside ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in a rogue child, it describes mischievous, badly behaved conduct.

clue.text: Immoderate vice, with sexes mixing

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: An orgy-like scene where vice involves both sexes mingling to an immoderate degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Going beyond reasonable limits is the shared sense of both words, as in excessive drinking.

clue.text: They'll take turns to steer fish onto waterways

indicators.note: in a down clue the fish is placed on top of the waterways

parts.note: the cod is a fish
rivers are waterways

explanation.surface: Fishermen take turns steering a boat along rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rally drivers share the wheel with partners who drive in shifts; those partners are co-drivers.

clue.text: Loose summary penned by the setter in more than one case

indicators.note: the summary is enclosed by the setter pronouns, as if shut in a pen

parts.words: the setter in more than one case
parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I (subject case) and ME (object case)
a précis is a summary

explanation.surface: A slack summary written by the compiler in several legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' means grammatical case; PRECIS goes inside the ME part of I ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose in the sense of not exact or vague, as in a loose translation.

clue.text: Obliged to provide tax before spring

indicators.note: the tax word comes first, ahead of the spring word

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
to bound is to spring or leap

explanation.surface: Someone forced to pay tax ahead of the spring season.
explanation.definitionFit: Being morally or legally compelled to act is what both words express.

clue.text: Herbivore perhaps runs into tanker

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the tanker word

parts.note: a bowser is a tanker carrying water or fuel
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A grazing animal perhaps blunders into a tanker.
explanation.walkthrough: A bowser is a tanker lorry for fuel or water.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal feeding on leaves and shoots browses, so a herbivore can be an example of one.

clue.text: Subject to election, king deposed

indicators.note: the king is removed from his place in the word for choice

parts.note: an election in its old sense is a choice, a pick
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is ousted after a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' tempts as a verb or as a royal subject; it is a theme. PICK loses its K to give PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject or theme under discussion.

clue.text: Starts using unorthodox tutor to cover diametrically opposite points

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the pair of compass points
an unorthodox arrangement of the letters of tutor

parts.note: north and south are opposite points of the compass

explanation.surface: An unconventional teacher begins using a method spanning opposite viewpoints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' is the anagram signal (giving TURTO), and 'to cover' wraps it round the two points; 'diametrically opposite' rules out east and west paired with north.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin to use or resort to something, as in taking up drink, is a phrasal-verb sense.

clue.text: Half of humour put online is rotten stuff

indicators.note: only the first three of the six letters of the humour word are kept

parts.note: comedy is humour
to post something is to put it on the internet

explanation.surface: A half-funny joke posted on the internet is garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed vegetable matter used as garden fertiliser is literally rotted stuff.

clue.text: Enchanting soldier in trenchcoat?

indicators.note: the soldier is placed inside the coat

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat such as a trenchcoat
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An alluring soldier wearing a trenchcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbinding charm is the adjectival sense, as in a magical evening.

clue.text: Follow the Tour de Yorkshire?

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is shortened to t'
a professional cycle race held each year in Yorkshire, an English county

explanation.surface: An invitation to follow the Yorkshire cycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire folk say "t'" for "the", so 'the' gives T; the Tour de Yorkshire is an annual cycle race in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To track or follow a path is to trace it.

clue.text: Middle Eastern king's backed by Italy and India

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: the king's name with its possessive is turned back to front

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king, and the possessive adds S
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern ruler gains the support of Italy and India.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARS reversed gives SRAEL, flanked by I and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being from the state of Israel makes one a Middle Eastern national.

clue.text: Initiate action as stage is delayed

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
late means delayed

explanation.surface: Someone takes action because one part of a trip is running late.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as LEG IS LATE. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass laws is to take formal action, which is what parliaments do to initiate change.

clue.text: Small dispute showing lack of flexibility

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a tiff is a small quarrel

explanation.surface: A minor argument reveals someone's inflexible nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid things will not bend, so lacking flexibility is a synonym.

clue.text: Gets control of temper — it's very important

parts.note: to corner a market is to get control of it
to tone is to moderate or temper

explanation.surface: Someone learns to manage their anger and declares it vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'temper' looks like a noun meaning anger; it is a verb, to moderate, giving TONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation stone bearing a building's weight is figuratively the most vital element of something.
